records.attribution_line: EU legislation from EUR-Lex (eur-lex.europa.eu). © European Union, 1998–2026. Consolidated texts are reused under CC BY 4.0. Extract only. Only the Official Journal of the European Union is authentic.
status_lines: Only European Union documents published in the Official Journal of the European Union are deemed authentic.
Extract only, where a single article or a capped passage is shown.
conditions: Documents with special conditions are title and link only: CELEX 32023R1803 and 32008R1126 (international accounting standards), every consolidated version of them, and any regulation whose title says it adopts or amends international accounting standards.
Third-party works inside a document, and content showing identifiable private individuals, may need their own permission.
not_covered: The EUR-Lex logo, which needs the prior consent of the Publications Office
Logos, names, trademarks, patents and registered designs
records.evidence: PDF of the legal notice page saved by the reader on 20 November 2026. Its filing location is tracked on TEC-746.
records.notes: The reader saved and supplied the page; an AI assistant working for the reader read it in full the same day. The notice says the legal documents published in EUR-Lex can be reused for commercial or non-commercial purposes unless otherwise specified, that the consolidated texts are licensed under CC BY 4.0 (acknowledge the source and indicate changes), and that EUR-Lex metadata is CC0. It sets no condition on linking and has no separate term on automated analysis. Regulation (EU) 2023/1803 says in recital 14 that the IFRS Foundation owns the copyright in the standards; Regulation (EC) No 1126/2008 says "Reproduction allowed within the European Economic Area". The eur-lex.europa.eu website returns an empty response to automated requests; the Publications Office endpoints do not. The attribution line and the exclusion rule were approved by the owner on 20 November 2026.

terms.title: Find Case Law, terms of use
Find Case Law, when you need permission

records.attribution_line: Judgment details from Find Case Law (caselaw.nationalarchives.gov.uk), The National Archives. Contains information licensed under the Open Justice - Licence v2.0. Linked, not reproduced: read the judgment on Find Case Law.
status_lines: Linked, not reproduced. Find Case Law holds the current version of a judgment, and a judgment can be revised or withdrawn.
Nothing here has official status, and neither the courts nor The National Archives endorse this use.
conditions: The licence does not cover computational analysis, "including indexing by search engines". The publisher says that means automated or algorithmic processing of large numbers of judgments, including using AI or large language models, text mining, building vector databases and bulk programmatic searching. That needs a separate licence from The National Archives, which is free to apply for.
A judgment may be copied one at a time as it is needed. Remove a copy that Find Case Law no longer publishes or has replaced with a revised version, and use the current version.

Comply with any judicial decision that restricts the use of personal data in a judgment. The licence is not a data sharing or processing agreement, so a re-user needs its own legal basis for the personal data.
Do not mislead about a judgment or its source, present it without regard to the dignity of the courts, or use it in a way that jeopardises the administration of justice.
No external indexing of documents. Follow robots.txt and the indexing directives on each document, and make a reasonable number of requests.
not_covered: Emblems and insignia of the courts and tribunals
Information that has not been published or disclosed under information access legislation
Third party rights the licensor is not authorised to license
Other intellectual property rights, including patents, trademarks and design rights
